req.title: Sessions use secret key
req.statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-034 requires that session cookies are signed with the SECRET_KEY from application config. Tests must verify: (1) a valid session cookie is issued and accepted when SECRET_KEY is set (positive/EP), (2) a cookie signed with a different SECRET_KEY is rejected (negative/NEG), and (3) the boundary where SECRET_KEY is the minimal non-empty string still produces a valid signed session (boundary/BVA). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes, exact cookie presence, exact session content, and verifying that tampering with the key causes rejection rather than acceptance.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_signed_with_secret_key_positive
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
Database initialised with fixture user (id=1, username=test, password=test)
actions: Inspect response status and that the session is accepted
expected: A 'session' cookie is present in the response
GET / with that cookie returns HTTP 200
Session cookie value is non-empty and iterable dot-separated Flask signed token
trace: R-FLASKR-034: session cookies signed with SECRET_KEY are accepted by the server
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'supersecret'})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_signed_with_secret_key_positive():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    cookie_value = session_cookies[0].split('=', 1)[1].split(';')[0]
    assert len(cookie_value) > 0
    parts = cookie_value.split('.')
    assert len(parts) == 3
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200

test_session_cookie_signed_with_secret_key_positive()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_rejected_when_signed_with_wrong_key_negative
preconditions: Two app instances created with different SECRET_KEYs
Database initialised with fixture user (id=1, username=test, password=test)
actions: POST /auth/login on app-A (SECRET_KEY='key-A') to obtain a signed session cookie
Send that cookie to app-B (SECRET_KEY='key-B') via GET /
Observe that app-B does not recognise the session (user not logged in)
expected: GET / on app-B returns HTTP 200 but session is not authenticated (no user_id in session)
Accessing /create on app-B with the foreign cookie returns HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-034: cookie signed with a different SECRET_KEY must not be accepted
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd1, path1 = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd1)
app_a = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path1, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-AAAA'})
with app_a.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd2)
app_b = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-BBBB'})
with app_b.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client_a = app_a.test_client()
client_b = app_b.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_rejected_when_signed_with_wrong_key_negative():
    r = client_a.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    raw_cookie = session_cookies[0].split(';')[0]
    r2 = client_b.get('/create', headers={'Cookie': raw_cookie})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_session_cookie_rejected_when_signed_with_wrong_key_negative()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_signed_with_minimal_one_char_secret_key_boundary
preconditions: App created with SECRET_KEY of exactly one character (boundary minimum non-empty key)
Database initialised with fixture user (id=1, username=test, password=test)
actions: Verify the session is accepted and user is treated as authenticated
expected: Session cookie is present and has three dot-separated parts (Flask itsdangerous format)
GET /create returns HTTP 200 (not a redirect to /auth/login), proving session accepted
trace: R-FLASKR-034: even a single-character SECRET_KEY must produce a valid signed session cookie

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'x'})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_signed_with_minimal_one_char_secret_key_boundary():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    cookie_value = session_cookies[0].split('=', 1)[1].split(';')[0]
    parts = cookie_value.split('.')
    assert len(parts) == 3
    assert all(len(p) > 0 for p in parts)
    r2 = client.get('/create')
    assert r2.status_code == 200

actions: Attempt GET /create without any session cookie

from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'testsecret'})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_absent_without_login_negative():
    r_index = client.get('/')
    assert r_index.status_code == 200
    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 302

tests.name: test_secret_key_loaded_from_config_state_transition
preconditions: App created with a specific SECRET_KEY value in test_config
actions: Verify app.config['SECRET_KEY'] equals the value passed in test_config
POST /auth/login to transition from anonymous to authenticated state
Verify session cookie is issued (state: authenticated)
POST /auth/logout to transition back to anonymous state
Verify /create redirects to login (state: anonymous again)
trace: R-FLASKR-034: SECRET_KEY is loaded from config and governs session signing across state transitions
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'my-test-secret'})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_secret_key_loaded_from_config_state_transition():
    assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'my-test-secret'
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    cookies = r_login.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
    session_cookies = [c for c in cookies if c.startswith('session=')]
    assert len(session_cookies) == 1
    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 200
    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302
    r_create2 = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create2.status_code == 302
    assert r_create2.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_secret_key_loaded_from_config_state_transition()
